clue.text: Put money on stock unit, a very good little earner

indicators.note: in a down-or-across charade 'on' sets one piece next to the other, here the money then the beast

parts.note: money in notes and coins is cash
a single head of livestock, one unit of the farm's stock, can be a cow

explanation.surface: A tip to bet on a single share, a little earner that pays handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks financial after 'Put money on', but it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a business or product that reliably brings in profit is called this, from a cow that keeps giving milk.

clue.text: Selection of superior quality

definitions.meaning: a pick or option taken from a range
as an adjective, describing top-grade produce such as fine cuts of meat

explanation.surface: A range of goods of the best quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: something picked out from alternatives, and an adjective for select, top-grade goods.

clue.text: First signs of spring have arrived, let's have a ball

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word spring, its first signs

parts.note: when you have arrived, you are here

explanation.surface: Spring's first signs are showing, so let's celebrate with a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First signs' is plural: take the first two letters, SP. 'ball' is the round object, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a round solid object is a globe or orb.

clue.text: Sing a carol, playing an instrument

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: Carol singing to the accompaniment of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' sounds musical with 'carol', but it signals rearranging SING A CAROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cor anglais is a woodwind instrument, a lower-pitched relative of the oboe.

clue.text: It enables one to turn one's hand to many things

definitions.text: It enables one to turn one's hand to many things

parts.words: It enables one to turn one's hand to many things
parts.note: the idiom for being versatile, read literally: the joint that lets the hand rotate

explanation.surface: A description of some skill that makes a person versatile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn one's hand to' means try many tasks, but here the hand literally turns, at the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the joint between forearm and hand lets the hand rotate.

clue.text: Criticise long dash

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: An order to find fault with a lengthy punctuation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' is not the punctuation line but style or flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: flamboyant style and verve can be called dash, a sense the French borrowing shares.

clue.text: It's up to Prior to provide an assortment

indicators.note: the letters of up to Prior are used to provide, make up, a new word

explanation.surface: A monastery's prior is given the job of arranging a mixed selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like 'earlier' or a monk, but is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: originally a mix of dried petals, now any miscellaneous medley or mixture.

clue.text: Absence of agreement regarding recess

parts.note: no, as in no entry, means an absence of something
OK signals agreement, yes

explanation.surface: Members failing to agree about taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a parliamentary break, but it is a small alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small corner or alcove set back into a wall is a recess.

clue.text: A potboiler?

parts.note: a potboiler is a cheap novel written for money, but read literally it is a pot that boils

explanation.surface: A query about a trashy novel churned out for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a large cooking vessel hung over a fire is literally a pot for boiling.

clue.text: All the same, the head makes a regular appearance

parts.note: even, as in even so, means all the same; also flat and uniform
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: The headmaster turns up regularly despite everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a person but a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: uniformity or smoothness, looking regular throughout.

clue.text: Alternative article in gold

indicators.note: 'in' here means the article sits inside the word for gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A different grammatical article set in a golden mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an alternative choice is a different one, the second of two.

clue.text: Offer fantastic reduction

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so the letters of reduction are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop promising a fantastic price cut on its goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offer' and 'reduction' read together as a sale; 'Offer' is the definition and 'fantastic' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to offer or put forward something new, such as a proposal or a product, is to bring it in.

clue.text: Enthronement of firm king's naught to the country

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
R stands for rex, Latin for king
naught, nothing, is the figure O
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A company monarch's crowning means nothing to the whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the ceremony of crowning a monarch and seating them on the throne.

clue.text: An imbibing of French port

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the first word swallows the French piece

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: Someone drinking a glass of French port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink after 'imbibing', but it is a harbour city in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Aden is a seaport city on the Gulf of Aden in Yemen.

clue.text: Either rises quickly or doesn't budge

definitions.meaning: gets to one's feet fast, read literally
holds firm and refuses to move or give way

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone who either jumps up or stays stubbornly put.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase gives opposite pictures: literally standing up fast, and idiomatically holding firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: getting up speedily, and the idiom for refusing to yield ground.

clue.text: Material allowances in cuts

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric, a material
rations are fixed allowances of food or goods

explanation.surface: Fabric quotas being reduced in a time of austerity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' reads as reductions to the allowances, but means wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: jagged tears or gashes in the skin are wounds of this kind.

clue.text: Unusually fierce sea battle ends with it

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An unusually ferocious naval engagement that finally stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea battle' reads as a phrase, but 'fierce sea' is the fodder and 'battle' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a truce or halt to shooting is how fighting comes to a stop.

clue.text: Art master's pets are dogs

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree, and the possessive adds S
a pet is a fit of sulking; tiffs are petty quarrels

explanation.surface: An art teacher's pets turn out to be dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' are not animals but sulks or squabbles, and the 's gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: mastiffs are a breed of large powerful guard dog.

clue.text: Wise step in the present era

indicators.note: 'in' puts the step inside the wise word

parts.note: sage means wise
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A wise move in today's world.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the period since space travel began is often called the current age of the rocket.

clue.text: Request for position in industry

definitions.meaning: a formal written request for a job
industry in the sense of diligence, hard and steady effort

explanation.surface: A job request for a post in manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'industry' looks like the sector of the job, but it is the second definition: diligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a formal bid for a job, and sustained diligent effort applied to a task.

clue.text: Vessel — showing its nationality?

parts.note: a ship shows its nationality by its flag
on, as in a play being on, means showing

explanation.surface: A ship at sea displaying its national colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a ship, and the ship flies its flag, but the answer is a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large bottle or jug for wine or cider is a vessel for holding drink.

clue.text: In radiography sickness has a cure

indicators.note: 'In' signals the answer sits inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An X-ray department where illness finds its treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: medicine or a remedy, the old word for the healing art and its drugs.

clue.text: Food on the turn?

definitions.meaning: hard ..., or ... alone, is plain food, especially ship's biscuit
in sailing, to change direction into the wind is a manoeuvre with this name

explanation.surface: Food that is going off and about to spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' suggests milk going sour; the sailing turn is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: coarse food such as ship's biscuit, and a sailing vessel's change of course.

clue.text: Old man from Maine so well in retirement

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
so and thus both mean therefore

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word for well is written back to front

parts.note: hale means healthy, well

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Maine who is keeping healthy in his retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns HALE into ELAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years, the byword for a very old man.

clue.text: Do they give feelings of elation to meteorologists?

definitions.text: Do they give feelings of elation to meteorologists?

parts.words: Do they give feelings of elation to meteorologists?
parts.note: feelings of elation are emotional peaks, but for weather forecasters the word means areas of high pressure

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes weather forecasters happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: euphoric moments, and to a forecaster, zones of high atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Cut price bargain

definitions.meaning: to make a small cut with scissors
something cheap at the price, a real bargain

explanation.surface: An advertisement for discounted, cut-price goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut price' reads as one phrase, but it splits after 'Cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a quick scissor cut, and an informal British word for something going cheap.

clue.text: Female relative in liaison, showing off

indicators.note: 'in' says the relative sits inside the word for a brief affair

parts.note: a fling is a short love affair, a liaison
an aunt is a parent's sister, a female relative

explanation.surface: An aunt caught up in an affair and making a show of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: displaying something ostentatiously is parading or showing it off.

clue.text: Soldier in ebbing sea gets support

indicators.note: 'in' places the soldier inside the turned word
an ebbing sea flows back, so the word sea is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written, before turning
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in a receding tide gets help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' says the sea flows backwards, so its letters are read in reverse before the soldier goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: under someone's protection or backing; the word came from the shield of Zeus.

clue.text: High point of religious architecture

parts.note: reads like the finest achievement of church building, but means the literal tallest part, the spire of a church

explanation.surface: An art historian naming the finest achievement of sacred building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High point' sounds like a figurative peak, but it is the physical tallest point of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the tall tower with a spire is literally the highest part of a church building.

clue.text: Like hell cats in a melee

indicators.note: a melee is a confused brawl, so the letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Cats caught in a scrap make a hellish din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like a link but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belonging to Satan, ruler of the underworld, so devilish or infernal.
